rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / ITERATORS AND GENERATORS / CHAPTER 22

slides.title: Iterators
slides.main: One protocol stands behind for, list, sum, zip, and your own classes.

items.title: Protocol
items.sub: Iterable gives an iterator, iterator gives values

slides.title: Iterable and iterator
slides.sub: iter() gives an iterator, next() the next value
slides.main: A list is iterable but not an iterator: next(list) fails.

body.text:
10 20
end
'list' object is not an iterator

slides.title: How for works
slides.main: Any for can be rewritten with while True, try, and except StopIteration.

slides.title: Single use
slides.main: File, zip, enumerate, map, filter are iterators; range is iterable and reusable.

body.text:
it = iter([1, 2, 3])
print(list(it))
print(list(it))        # exhausted
r = range(3)
print(list(r), list(r))

slides.title: Custom iterator
slides.main: Raise StopIteration at the right moment, or the loop never ends.

slides.title: Reusable iterable
slides.sub: __iter__ creates a new iterator each time
slides.main: Collections are iterable; iterators are created on demand.

body.text: If __iter__ returns self, the class becomes single-use.

slides.title: Helpers
slides.sub: enumerate, zip, reversed, next with default
slides.main: What one consumer understands, all do: list, tuple, sum, max, join, in.

slides.title: Unpacking and consumers
slides.sub: Star, sum, max, next with default
slides.main: next(stream, default) safely takes one element: handy for the first match.

body.text:
a, *rest = iter([1, 2, 3, 4])
print(a, rest)
print(*[1, 2, 3])
print(sum(x for x in range(5)), max(iter([3, 9, 2])))
gen = (n for n in [5, 8, 12] if n > 6)
print(next(gen), next(gen, None), next(gen, None))

slides.title: Laziness
slides.main: Instead of compute everything, then select: describe a pipeline, pull one by one.

body.text:
big = range(10**12)
print(len(big), big[-1])
nums = map(str, range(3))
print(type(nums).__name__)     # nothing computed yet
print(list(nums))

slides.title: Infinite iterators
slides.main: Always limit an infinite stream: break, a counter, or a condition.

body.text: list(Fib()) never returns and eats all memory.

slides.title: Dictionaries and iteration
slides.main: Never change a dictionary's size while looping: the iterator loses consistency.

body.text:
a b [('a', 1), ('b', 2)]
['b', 'a']
dictionary changed size during iteration

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: An iterator is a single-use cursor; an iterable is a source of fresh cursors.

body.text:
f = open("demo.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8")
f.write("1\n2\n")
f.close()

f = open("demo.txt", encoding="utf-8")
print(list(f))
print(list(f))        # a file is an iterator: second pass is empty
f.close()
Also: next(list), iterable returning self, no StopIteration, list(infinite).

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: An iterator is a single-use cursor; an iterable is a source of fresh cursors.

items.title: Own class
items.sub: Reusable: iter creates a new iterator

items.title: Laziness
items.sub: Memory for one item; limit infinite ones
